Definition: middle voice from G1909 and G2990; to lose out of mind; by implication, to neglect:--(be) forget(-ful of).
BiblicalUsage: Epilanthanomai means to forget, to lose out of mind, to neglect. The disciples forgot to take bread; not one sparrow is forgotten before God; God is not unrighteous to forget your work and labour of love; be not forgetful to entertain strangers; and the hearer who forgets is like a man who looks in a glass and goes away.
TheologicalSignificance: God never forgets a sparrow or a labour of love, and I must not forget the stranger or the word I heard. I believe the word cuts both ways and comforts both ways, and remembering is a duty I owe in both directions.
